extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, geometers, and astronomers (students and practitioners of classical mechanics and conic-section constructions)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric propositions, lemmas and problems giving constructions and analytic methods to describe conic trajectories (parabola, ellipse, hyperbola), locate points at given times, and relate kinematic quantities under central forces. Emphasis on compass-and-straightedge constructions, similarity arguments, and area-time correspondences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. I — parallelogram and equal rectangles from given conic section
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc si datur parallelogrammum I K L M, circa datam sectionem conicam descripitum, dabitur rectangulum KQxME, ut & huic sequale rectangulum KHxMF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a conic section and a constructed parallelogram about it, one may form rectangles (KQ×ME and KH×MF) equal by using similarity of triangles (KQH and MFE). The corollary records the proportional equalities to be used in constructing equal-area rectangles associated to contact points and abscissae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. II — equality of rectangles from intersecting tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Si sexta ducatur tangens eg tangentibus K I, MI occurrens in e; rectangulum KQxME sequabitur rectangulo KqxMe; eritque KQ ad ME ut Kq ad ME, & divisim ut Qq ad Ee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an additional tangent intersects others, corresponding products of segments (rectangles) follow equalities and proportionalities. Use these proportional relations to transfer segment products when tangents meet at new points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. III — line through midpoints passes through centre of conic
rubrics_metrics.description: Si E q jungantur & biseceantur, & recta per puncta bisectionum agatur, transibit haec per centrum sectionis conicae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pairs of corresponding contact points are joined and bisected, the straight line through those bisection points passes through the centre of the conic. This provides a construction for locating the centre from tangent/contact data (proved via equality of segments and lemmas).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXVII / PROBLEMA XIX — construct trajectory tangent to five given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Trajectoriam describere quæ rectas quinque positione datas continget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given five tangents (positions), construct the trajectory by: (1) forming appropriate quadrilaterals of four tangents whose diagonals bisect, (2) finding the concurrence (centre) as intersection of bisector-lines, (3) for a chosen tangent, draw a parallel at such a distance that the centre lies midway between parallels — this parallel will be a tangent to the required trajectory, (4) locate other contact points by intersecting parallels and applying corollary lemmas, and finally use previous construction (prob. xiv) to describe the trajectory. The scholium notes treatment of asymptotes as tangents at infinity and describes how to find axes and umbilics from the centre via angular constructions and normals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding axes and umbilics from a given trajectory centre
rubrics_metrics.description: Postquam trajectoria descripta est, invenire licet axes & umbilicos ejus hac methodo ... Si describant altera angulorum crura C N, B N, concursus suus K vel ky circulum BGKC. Sit circuli hujus centrum O ... demitte normalem O H circulo occurrentem va K & L. ... Unde si detur trajectoriae centrum, dabuntur axes. Hisce autem datis, umbilici sunt in promptu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the centre O of a trajectory, produce the axes by constructing conjugate angular crura, producing a circle through their intersection, dropping normals from O to the regulating line M N to find intersections with the constructed circle; these yield axes (major/minor) and hence umbilici. Use perpendicularity relations: axes are mutually perpendicular; deduce major/minor axes by relative positions of intersection points.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEMMA XXVI — triangle of given shape & magnitude tangent to three given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Trianguli specie & magnitudine dati tres angulos ad rectas totidem positione datas, quæ non sunt omnes parallelæ, singulos ad singulas ponere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given three infinite lines in specified positions AB, AC, BC and three angles (shape & size) to be placed so each triangle angle is tangent to the corresponding line: construct three circular segments on triangle sides equal to the given vertex angles; complete to full circles, find intersections of the first two circles, take proportions along connecting lines to place center points, and draw arcs/circles to obtain a triangle similar and equal to the reference triangle. Use similarity and proportional placement of points to ensure tangency to the given lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXVIII / PROBLEMA XX — trajectory of given species & magnitude with parts cut by three given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Trajectoriam specie & magnitudine datam describere, cujus partes datae rectis tribus positione datis interjacebunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to previous lemma: choose a triangle D E F whose sides DE, EF, DF are placed with prescribed angles to the three given lines (per lemma XXVI). Around that triangle describe a trajectory curve similar and equal to the given curve D E F; this ensures that its parts are cut in the given proportions by the three given position-lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEMMA XXVII — trapezium of given species with angles tangent to four given lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Trapezium specie datum describere, cujus anguli ad rectas quatuor positione datas, quæ neque omnes parallelae sunt, neque ad commune punctum convergunt, singuli ad singulas consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given four position-lines AB, AD, BD, CE and a trapezium shape FGHI, construct three circular segments on sides through F that subtend angles equal to the given incidences; extend segments to full circles, find centers, take proportional points on a line through centers, describe a fourth circle through that point cutting the third circle appropriately, and map back via similarity to construct trapezium similar to FGHI whose angles touch the four given lines. Auxiliary constructions use intersections of circle arcs and proportional divisions (numerous stepwise geometric steps provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary to Lemma XXVII — drawing a straight line with parts between four given lines in prescribed proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc recta duci potest cujus partes, rectis quatuor positione datis dato ordine interjectae, datam habebunt proportionem ad invicem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By enlarging angles of the trapezium until adjacent sides become collinear, the construction yields a straight line whose successive segments intercept between the four given lines are in the required proportions to one another. Practical construction methods (extensions, parallels, and proportional divisions) are given as expedients.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXIX / PROBLEMA XXI — trajectory similar to given curve with parts cut by four lines in order and proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Trajectoriam specie datam describere quæ a rectis quatuor positione datis in partes secabitur ordine, specie & proportione datas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct (per lemma xxvii) a trapezium fghi similar to a given trapezium FGHI whose angles are tangent to the four given lines in the prescribed order; then around this trapezium describe a curve similar to the given curve FGHI to obtain the required trajectory. The scholium gives an alternate construction using produced lines, proportional angles and chord placements enabling a step-by-step practical construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXX / PROBLEMA XXII — locate body on parabola at given time via area-time correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis in data trajectoria parabolica moti invenire locum ad tempus assignatum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The area A P S (area abscindenda from the parabola with vertex A and umbilicus S) is proportional to the elapsed time. Construction: bisect AS, erect a perpendicular such that GH^2 relates to a given quantity M, draw a circle with center H and radius HS; this circle will cut the parabola in point P — the body's locus at the given time. Corollaries: proportions of GH to AS correspond to time ratios for different arcs; relations of velocities (e.g., velocity of point H on the circle vs velocity at parabola vertex in ratio 3:8) follow from the construction. Procedure allows also inversion: given an arc, find time.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEMMA XXVIII — nonexistence of an oval with area-abscissa given by finite algebraic equation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nulla extat figura ovalis cujus area, rectis pro lubitu abscissa, possit per aequationes numero terminorum ac dimensionum finitas generaliter inveniri.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: considering a point that revolves and traces an infinite-spiral, intersections of a line with the spiral are infinite; therefore, a finite polynomial (finite-term) equation cannot in general express the abscissa-area relation. Consequences: area of an ellipse described from the umbilicus is not expressible by a finite algebraic equation in time; such curves are 'geometrically irrational'. Use this to justify necessity of transcendental/series methods for certain orbital problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXXI / PROBLEMA XXIII — locate body on ellipse at given time via trochoid-circle mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis in data trajectoria elliptica moti invenire locum ad tempus assignatum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a trochoid by revolving a circle GE F (center O) while a point on its rim (A) describes a trochoid ALI. Choose a point GK on the circle so that GK:perimeter(GE) equals the time for the ellipse-arc AP divided by the time of one revolution. Erect perpendicular KL meeting the trochoid at Z; a line through L parallel to KG meets the ellipse at the required locus P. Scholium: when exact construction is difficult, use an analytic/series approximation: compute an auxiliary angle (approx. 57.29578 degrees per unit), a length L in inverse proportion, then iteratively compute correction angles E, G, I,... building a rapidly convergent infinite series AOQ + E + G + I + ... whose cosine and sine give corrected abscissa and ordinate to locate P. The method generalizes to hyperbola with logarithmic tables and iterative chord corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXXII / PROBLEMA XXIV — distances for straight-line ascent/descent under inverse-square centripetal force via conic-area limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Posto quocunque vis centripeta sit reciproce proportionalis quadrato distantiae locorum a centro, spatia definire quæ corpus recta cadendo datis temporibus describit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case analysis: if the trajectory section is an ellipse, area segments A S D, etc., are proportional to time; as the ellipse's minor width tends to zero the orbit tends to a straight line and the corresponding area gives the distance AC that the body falls in the given time. Similar limiting constructions for hyperbola and parabola obtain distances for rectilinear descent by taking appropriate limiting areas and dropping perpendiculars from constructed points to axes. Use area-time proportional constructions from the associated conic to obtain straight-line distances under inverse-square attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXXIII / THEOREMA IX — velocity relation between straight-line fall and circular motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporis cadentis velocitas in loco quovis C est ad velocitatem corporis centro B intervallo BC circulum describentis, in subduplicata ratione quam AC ... habet ad semidiametrum principalem k AB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given conic sections and constructed diameters, bisect AB, draw a tangent PT to the conic through P that meets the common diameter; by earlier corollaries the velocity in the conic at P compared to the circular velocity about the same centre S at radius SP is in the subduplicate ratio of certain products/rectangles involving SP and distances along constructed diameters. By taking limits (mapping the conic to a straight line) the result gives the velocity of rectilinear descent relative to circular motion in a subduplicate ratio of AC to the semidiameter (AO or AB). The theorem provides an explicit proportional law (subduplicate ratio) to compare linear-fall velocities with circular orbital velocities under inverse-square centripetal force.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO XXXIV / THEOREMA X — special case for parabola: velocity relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Si figura B E D parabola est, dico quod corporis cadentis velocitas in loco quovis C est aequalis est velocitati qua corpus centro B dimidio intervalli sui B C circulum uniformiter describere potest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the case of a parabolic figure, the theorem asserts that the falling body's speed at any point C equals the speed that would allow a body at B to describe uniformly a circle whose radius is half the interval BC. This gives a concrete proportional equivalence (a specific subcase of the general velocity-comparison theorem) useful for inverse-square-force motion when the conic is a parabola.
